docRequirement: A hook process on four events must find a writable file path in `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`, and `export` lines appended to that file must take effect in every later Bash command of the session. hooks.md:1021 — "SessionStart hooks have access to the `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` environment variable, which provides a file path where you can persist environment variables for subsequent Bash commands." hooks.md:1023 — "To set individual environment variables, write `export` statements to `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`. Use append (`>>`) to preserve variables set by other hooks". hooks.md:1056 — "Any variables written to this file will be available in all subsequent Bash commands that Claude Code executes during the session." Scope is closed at hooks.md:1059 — "`CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` is available for SessionStart, [Setup](#setup), [CwdChanged](#cwdchanged), and [FileChanged](#filechanged) hooks. Other hook types don't have access to this variable." — repeated per event at hooks.md:1116 (Setup), :2433 (CwdChanged), :2509 (FileChanged). cloud-environments.md:392 only cross-references this: "To persist environment variables for subsequent Bash commands, write to the file at `$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`. See [SessionStart hooks](/docs/en/hooks#sessionstart) for details."

divergence: Not a key-name or value mismatch — the whole channel is missing, in both directions. Inbound: no `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` (nor a `NESSY_ENV_FILE` of our own) is exported to any hook process, and no per-session file is created for one to point at, so on all four documented events the variable is unset. Outbound: even if a hook wrote such a file, nothing reads it — the Bash tool's command string reaches `/bin/sh -lc` verbatim (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:3647-3651) with no host-authored source preamble, and the host merges no parsed env into the spawn (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:5201-5214). Two things this is NOT: it is not the SessionStart `context-only` decision classification (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-decision-contract.ts:85-90) — `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` is an inbound env var naming a file, not a stdout field, so widening SessionStart's decision surface would not close it; and it is not the exec-form placeholder list at packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:161-170, which the filed evidence mis-cited as "the env allowlist".

change.what: New module owning the per-session env file. `HOOK_ENV_FILE_EVENTS: ReadonlySet<AgentEvent> = new Set(['SessionStart','Setup','CwdChanged','FileChanged'])`, carrying hooks.md:1059 verbatim as the reason so the set cannot silently widen. `hookEnvFilePath(workspaceId, sessionId)` = `join(getSessionDirPath(workspaceId, sessionId), 'hook-env.sh')` (helper at packages/shared/src/sessions/storage.ts:76; `ensureSessionDir` at :89 already creates the directory). `ensureHookEnvFile(...)` creates the file mode 0600 if absent and returns its absolute path — idempotent, so no lifecycle wiring is needed. Truncate it once per Pi runtime start, not per event: a resumed session re-runs SessionStart with `source: 'resume'` and would otherwise accumulate duplicate `export` lines. The file MUST live under the session storage dir, never inside the workspace: the workspace root is writable by the sandboxed Bash tool, and a model-writable env file would be an env-injection channel into every later command.

Give `buildHookCommandEnv` a fourth parameter `envFilePath?: string` and, when `HOOK_ENV_FILE_EVENTS.has(event)` and the path is present, set `NESSY_ENV_FILE` plus the compat alias `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` — placed AFTER the `SAFE_INHERITED_ENV_KEYS` loop (:56-59) and BEFORE the `actionEnv` merge (:76-78), so `expandEnvVars` can reference it and a bundle still cannot shadow it. This is the same two-name pattern already used for `NESSY_PROJECT_DIR`/`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`. Thread the same option through `runHookCommand`'s `options` (:653-664) for the direct/legacy authority. Do NOT add `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` to `EXEC_FORM_PATH_PLACEHOLDERS` (:161-170): hooks.md documents only the plugin-root/project-dir placeholders for exec-form substitution.

Two edits inside the runner. At :4344 pass `ensureHookEnvFile(managed.workspace.id, managed.id)` as the new fourth argument to `buildHookCommandEnv` when `HOOK_ENV_FILE_EVENTS.has(options.event)`. At :4463 add that file's parent directory to `additionalWritableRoots` for those same events — without it the hook cannot write the file at all: the spawn runs `profile: 'workspace'` with `workspaceRoot: options.cwd` (:4477-4478) and today's only extra writable root is the plugin data path. Keep the env var out of the environment on every other event so hooks.md:1059's "Other hook types don't have access" holds.

Read the file back on the Bash path. In the host rebuild, when `request.semanticId` is `'bash'` or `'bash_background'` AND the invocation matches the wrapper shape the subprocess builds (`command` = `/bin/sh` with `args === ['-lc', cmd]`, or `cmd.exe` with `['/d','/s','/c', cmd]` — verify the shape, never rewrite blindly, or a plugin-MCP or LSP start would be corrupted), replace the command argument with a host-authored preamble: POSIX `[ -f <file> ] && . <file>; <cmd>`, win32 `if exist <file> call <file> && <cmd>`. `<file>` is the host-owned `hookEnvFilePath(...)`, never a child-supplied value. Do the rewrite AFTER `pickSupervisedChildStartFields` (:5203), alongside the existing host-owned `PATH`/plugin-env merge (:5187-5212). Parsing the file into `env` instead is NOT sufficient: the documented recipes are `export PATH="$PATH:./node_modules/.bin"` (hooks.md:1031) and a `comm -13` diff of `export -p` output (hooks.md:1050), both of which need shell evaluation. Also mint/truncate the file where the Pi runtime starts so Setup — emitted before instructions and session start — finds it.

Two table-driven cases: on each of the four events the built env carries `NESSY_ENV_FILE` and `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` set to the minted path; on a representative fifth event (`PreToolUse`) neither key is present. Add one host-level case asserting the Bash preamble is prepended for `semanticId: 'bash'` and that a non-shell start (a plugin-MCP command) is left byte-identical — the shape guard is the part that can silently corrupt an unrelated spawn.

blastRadius: Crosses a process-lifecycle boundary and therefore trips this repo's risk triggers. (1) `buildHookCommandEnv` has four callers (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts, packages/shared/src/automations/index.ts, packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts) and codegraph reports no covering test today — a new optional parameter is source-compatible, but the two execution authorities must be changed together or the env var appears on one path only. (2) The supervised-process request is a host/child trust boundary: `pickSupervisedChildStartFields` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/process-supervisor-port.ts:124-140) is the deliberate allowlist that stops a subprocess smuggling `env`, so the preamble must be composed on the HOST side of it; doing it in packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:3647 instead would put the file path inside the child. (3) The rewritten command line is no longer byte-identical to the line the permission gate judged and the execution receipt records (`appendPiExecutionReceipt` / `environmentDigest` in packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:734-740) — the preamble is host-authored and constant, so it grants the model no new authority, but the receipt/approval-card text changes and the exec-form comment at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4337-4343 states the repo's rule that the judged line and the run line must match. Decide and record which of the two the receipt shows. (4) Sandbox surface: the env file must sit outside every model-writable root, and the hook spawn needs it added to `additionalWritableRoots`, which feeds `resolveProcessIsolation` and the darwin/linux sandbox profiles. (5) Imported-plugin paths: format-adapters map Claude and Codex hooks onto all four events (packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:373-393, packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:124-183), so any Claude bundle's hook is a consumer the moment this lands. (6) Tests touching the area: packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.process-supervisor.test.ts, packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.test.ts, packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/hook-stdout-context.test.ts, packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-bash-output.test.ts, packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/plugin-bin-path.test.ts. No wire DTO or persisted schema changes if the file stays a host-side implementation detail; adding it to `SupervisedProcessStartRequest` would make it one.
userImpact: Concrete and silent. A user installs a Claude plugin (or writes a hook) whose SessionStart/Setup/CwdChanged/FileChanged script follows the documented recipe — `if [ -n "$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE" ]; then echo 'export NODE_ENV=production' >> "$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE"; fi`, or the `nvm use 20` / venv / direnv variant. On Nessy the variable is unset, the guard is false, the hook exits 0, and it does literally nothing: no error notice, no transcript entry, nothing in the hook error surface. The user then watches every Bash tool call run without the environment their setup hook was supposed to establish — wrong Node or Python version, missing `./node_modules/.bin` on PATH, missing project env — and the agent reports a toolchain mismatch with no pointer to the cause. The un-guarded variant is worse in a different way: `>> "$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE"` on an empty path fails, the hook exits non-zero, and the user gets a bare `<hook name> hook error` notice with no explanation of why. Nothing surfaces the real reason on either shape today.
